name: Chicago
summary: The big city of the Midwest on Lake Michigan: a skyline of landmark architecture along the river, free lakefront beaches, the elevated L, blues and improv, deep-dish and Italian beef, and neighborhoods with fierce loyalties from Rogers Park to the South Side.

curated-2026-10.title: Chicago places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Chicago (O'Hare and Midway)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available.

neighborhoods.name: The Loop
neighborhoods.summary: The downtown ringed by the elevated tracks: trading floors on LaSalle, the theater district on State and Randolph, Millennium Park and the Art Institute on Michigan Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: River North
neighborhoods.summary: Galleries turned into steakhouses, clubs and glassy rental towers north of the river, with the Merchandise Mart and the tourist deep-dish rooms.

neighborhoods.name: Streeterville
neighborhoods.summary: High-rises between the Magnificent Mile and the lake, home to Navy Pier, the Northwestern hospital campus and its medical students.

neighborhoods.name: Gold Coast
neighborhoods.summary: Old money mansions and doorman co-ops off Lake Shore Drive, with Oak Street boutiques and the late-night Rush and Division bar strip a block away.

neighborhoods.name: Lincoln Park & Old Town
neighborhoods.summary: Leafy greystones and brick two-flats around the free zoo and the big lakefront park, with DePaul students, Steppenwolf and Second City on Wells Street.

neighborhoods.name: Lakeview & Wrigleyville
neighborhoods.summary: Vintage courtyard buildings, the ivy at Wrigley Field and its bars, and Northalsted, the city's historic LGBTQ+ neighborhood.

neighborhoods.name: Wicker Park & Bucktown
neighborhoods.summary: The six-corner crossroads of Milwaukee, North and Damen: boutiques, record shops, cocktail bars and the elevated 606 trail, once the heart of Polish Chicago.

neighborhoods.name: Ukrainian Village & West Town
neighborhoods.summary: Gold-domed churches, Ukrainian bakeries and dive bars along Chicago Avenue, with old workers' cottages between them.

neighborhoods.name: Logan Square
neighborhoods.summary: Wide boulevards and greystones around the eagle-topped Centennial Monument, with a Sunday farmers market, a strong Latino history and a young, creative crowd.

neighborhoods.name: Humboldt Park
neighborhoods.summary: The center of Puerto Rican Chicago: a vast park with a lagoon and boathouse, and Paseo Boricua on Division Street between two giant steel flags.

neighborhoods.name: West Loop & Fulton Market
neighborhoods.summary: Meatpacking warehouses turned into Restaurant Row, tech offices and hotels, with the United Center to the west and the commuter stations to the east.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy & University Village
neighborhoods.summary: Taylor Street's red-sauce restaurants and lemonade stands beside the UIC campus and the Illinois Medical District hospitals.

neighborhoods.name: Pilsen
neighborhoods.summary: Mexican Chicago's cultural heart: murals on every viaduct, panaderias and taquerias along 18th Street and old Bohemian brick buildings full of artists' studios.

neighborhoods.name: Little Village
neighborhoods.summary: La Villita: 26th Street, one of the busiest Mexican shopping streets in the country, under a welcome arch, with families in brick bungalows and two-flats.

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown
neighborhoods.summary: Wentworth Avenue and the newer Chinatown Square under the red gate, with dim sum, bakeries and Ping Tom park on the river.

neighborhoods.name: South Loop & Museum Campus
neighborhoods.summary: Former rail yards turned towers and townhouses, with Printers Row, Columbia College students and the museums and Soldier Field on the lake.

neighborhoods.name: Bronzeville
neighborhoods.summary: The "Black Metropolis" of the Great Migration: greystones and mansions along King Drive, the jazz and blues history of 47th Street, and the IIT campus to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Hyde Park
neighborhoods.summary: The University of Chicago's gothic quads, bookstores and co-op flats between Washington Park and the lake, a famously integrated, intellectual corner of the South Side.

neighborhoods.name: Bridgeport
neighborhoods.summary: Old Irish South Side, home of five mayors and the White Sox, now mixed with Chinese and Mexican families, art spaces and corner taverns.

neighborhoods.name: Andersonville
neighborhoods.summary: The old Swedish strip of Clark Street: independent shops, Belgian beer, a large LGBTQ+ community and a water tower painted with the Swedish flag.

neighborhoods.name: Uptown
neighborhoods.summary: Grand old theaters and ballrooms, the Green Mill, Vietnamese Argyle Street and Montrose Beach, in one of the most mixed neighborhoods in the city.

neighborhoods.name: Rogers Park & West Ridge
neighborhoods.summary: The far North Side by the lake: Loyola's campus, small beaches at the end of nearly every street, and Devon Avenue's South Asian shops to the west.

neighborhoods.name: Evanston
neighborhoods.summary: The first suburb north on the lake: Northwestern University, a walkable downtown, big old houses and fenced beaches that charge a summer token.

neighborhoods.name: Oak Park
neighborhoods.summary: The village just west of the city line, with the world's largest collection of Frank Lloyd Wright buildings, Hemingway's birthplace and tree-lined family streets.

transit.name: CTA Red Line
transit.summary: The busiest L line, 24 hours a day, from Howard through the State Street subway to 95th Street, stopping at Wrigley Field and the White Sox park.

transit.name: CTA Blue Line
transit.summary: A 24-hour line from O'Hare Airport through Logan Square, Wicker Park and the Dearborn subway to the Loop and on west to Forest Park.

transit.name: CTA Brown Line
transit.summary: Elevated line from Kimball through Ravenswood, Lakeview and Old Town around the Loop, the classic rattling ride past back porches.

transit.name: CTA Green Line
transit.summary: From Oak Park and the West Side over Lake Street through the Loop and south through Bronzeville.

transit.name: CTA Orange Line
transit.summary: From Midway Airport past Bridgeport and Chinatown to the Loop.

transit.name: CTA Pink Line
transit.summary: From Cicero through Little Village and Pilsen to the Loop.

transit.name: CTA Purple Line
transit.summary: From Linden in Wilmette through Evanston to Howard, with rush-hour express trains running on to the Loop.

transit.name: Metra
transit.summary: Commuter rail from Union Station, Ogilvie, LaSalle Street and Millennium Station to the suburbs, including the Electric line to Hyde Park.

transit.name: South Shore Line
transit.summary: The interurban from Millennium Station through Hyde Park to Gary and South Bend in Indiana.

transit.name: CTA buses
transit.summary: A grid of bus routes on nearly every major street, including the lakefront express buses along Lake Shore Drive.

transit.name: Pace suburban buses
transit.summary: Buses across the suburbs, including Evanston and Oak Park.

transit.name: Chicago Water Taxi and Shoreline water taxis
transit.summary: River boats between the commuter stations, Michigan Avenue and Chinatown, and lake taxis between Navy Pier and the Museum Campus in summer.

transit.name: Divvy
transit.summary: Blue bikes and e-bikes docked across the city and Evanston.

places.name: Art Institute of Chicago
places.summary: One of the great art museums, guarded by two bronze lions: Seurat's "La Grande Jatte", "Nighthawks", "American Gothic" and the Thorne miniature rooms.

places.name: Millennium Park
places.summary: Cloud Gate (the Bean), the Crown Fountain faces that spit water at children, gardens and free summer concerts at the Pritzker Pavilion.

places.name: Maggie Daley Park
places.summary: Playgrounds and climbing walls in summer and a looping ice-skating ribbon in winter, just east of Millennium Park.

places.name: Buckingham Fountain
places.summary: The great tiered fountain in Grant Park, with water shows on the hour and a lit display after dark in the warm months.

places.name: Chicago Riverwalk
places.summary: A promenade along the main branch of the river under the bridges, with wine bars, kayak rentals and tour boats.

places.name: Architecture river cruise
places.summary: A ninety-minute boat tour down the river with a guide naming every tower, from the Wrigley Building to Willis Tower.

places.name: Skydeck at Willis Tower
places.summary: Glass boxes on the 103rd floor of the tower everyone still calls the Sears Tower.

places.name: Chicago Cultural Center
places.summary: The old public library, free to enter, with the world's largest Tiffany glass dome, exhibitions and lunchtime concerts.

places.name: Chicago Theatre
places.summary: The 1921 movie palace under the famous red CHICAGO marquee on State Street, now for comedians and concerts.

places.name: Symphony Center
places.summary: Home of the Chicago Symphony Orchestra on Michigan Avenue across from the Art Institute.

places.name: Goodman Theatre
places.summary: The city's oldest nonprofit theater, in the Randolph Street theater district, with a "Christmas Carol" every December.

places.name: Harold Washington Library Center
places.summary: The huge central public library with owls on the roof, a winter garden on the ninth floor and free music studios.

places.name: The Berghoff
places.summary: German restaurant on Adams Street since 1898, with its own root beer, schnitzel and a standing bar.

places.name: Intelligentsia Coffee (Randolph Street)
places.summary: The Chicago roaster's downtown bar by Millennium Park, full of office workers before nine.

places.name: Pizzeria Uno
places.summary: The 1943 basement room where deep-dish began, at Ohio and Wabash; expect a wait and a forty-minute bake.

places.name: Lou Malnati's (River North)
places.summary: The local favorite for deep-dish with a buttery crust and a sausage patty that covers the whole pie.

places.name: Portillo's (River North)
places.summary: Big, loud, fast hot dogs, Italian beef and chocolate cake shakes in a Prohibition-themed hall.

places.name: Mr. Beef on Orleans
places.summary: A no-frills Italian beef counter, decades older than the TV show it inspired.

places.name: Frontera Grill
places.summary: Rick Bayless's regional Mexican restaurant on Clark Street, with moles and margaritas.

places.name: Gene & Georgetti
places.summary: Old-school steakhouse in a frame house under the L since 1941, with tuxedoed waiters.

places.name: Andy's Jazz Club
places.summary: Long-running jazz room on Hubbard Street with two sets a night and a supper menu.

places.name: East Bank Club
places.summary: A huge riverside athletic club with pools, courts and a well-known members' scene.

places.name: Art on the Mart
places.summary: Projected digital art across the river face of the Merchandise Mart after dark, best watched from the Riverwalk.

places.name: Navy Pier
places.summary: A long pier into the lake with the Centennial Wheel, boat tours, a children's museum and summer fireworks.

places.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
places.summary: Contemporary art museum off Michigan Avenue, with a summer farmers market on its plaza.

places.name: 360 Chicago
places.summary: The observation deck on the 94th floor of the former John Hancock Center, with the tilting TILT windows.

places.name: Ohio Street Beach
places.summary: A small sheltered beach by Navy Pier where open-water swimmers train along the buoy line.

places.name: Chicago Shakespeare Theater
places.summary: Thrust-stage theater at Navy Pier doing Shakespeare and musicals.

places.name: Water Tower and Magnificent Mile
places.summary: The castle-like 1869 Water Tower that survived the Great Fire, and the flagship stores of North Michigan Avenue around it.

places.name: Billy Goat Tavern
places.summary: Underground grill-and-bar on lower Michigan Avenue, of the "cheezborger, cheezborger" sketch and the Cubs curse.

places.name: Starbucks Reserve Roastery
places.summary: Five floors of roasting machines, bars and tourists on the Magnificent Mile.

places.name: Oak Street Beach
places.summary: Sand right under the high-rises where Lake Shore Drive bends, busy and glamorous on hot weekends.

places.name: Gibsons Bar & Steakhouse
places.summary: Rush Street steakhouse with huge martinis, slabs of cake and a well-dressed crowd.

places.name: Rush and Division
places.summary: The "Viagra Triangle" strip of bars and clubs where Rush meets Division and Elm, loud until late.

places.name: The Original Pancake House (Bellevue)
places.summary: Weekend lines for the oven-baked apple pancake and the Dutch baby.

places.name: International Museum of Surgical Science
places.summary: Odd, absorbing medical history in a lakefront mansion: trepanned skulls, iron lungs and amputation kits.

places.name: Newberry Library
places.summary: Independent research library facing Washington Square, the old "Bughouse Square" of soapbox speakers.

places.name: Giordano's (Rush Street)
places.summary: Stuffed pizza with a top crust and a cheese pull for the photos.

places.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
places.summary: A free zoo in the park since 1868, with gorillas, lions and ZooLights in winter.

places.name: Lincoln Park Conservatory
places.summary: Victorian glass houses of palms, ferns and orchids, warm and green in January.

places.name: North Avenue Beach
places.summary: The big volleyball beach with a boat-shaped beach house and the skyline view south.

places.name: Lakefront Trail
places.summary: Eighteen miles of separated paths for runners and cyclists along the lake from Ardmore to 71st Street.

places.name: The Second City
places.summary: The improv and sketch theater on Wells Street that trained generations of comedians, with a free improv set after the late show.

places.name: Steppenwolf Theatre
places.summary: Ensemble theater on Halsted Street known for intense, actor-driven productions.

places.name: Kingston Mines
places.summary: Two stages of blues alternating all night on Halsted Street, open until four on weekends.

places.name: Chicago History Museum
places.summary: The city's story from the Great Fire to the Cubs, with the first L car and a Chicago-style hot dog "sensory" exhibit.

places.name: The Wiener's Circle
places.summary: Late-night char-dogs on Clark Street, where customers and staff trade insults across the counter at 2 a.m.

places.name: Old Town Ale House
places.summary: A beloved dive across from Second City, its walls hung with the owner's satirical paintings.

places.name: Alinea
places.summary: Grant Achatz's tasting-menu restaurant, theatrical and very expensive, on Halsted Street.

places.name: The Bourgeois Pig Cafe
places.summary: Creaky Victorian coffeehouse on Fullerton full of DePaul students and literary-named sandwiches.

places.name: Wrigley Field
places.summary: The Cubs' 1914 ballpark with ivy on the outfield walls, a hand-turned scoreboard and rooftop bleachers across the street.

places.name: Murphy's Bleachers
places.summary: The bar across from the Wrigley bleacher gate, packed before and after every game.

places.name: Ann Sather
places.summary: Swedish diner on Belmont famous for its gooey cinnamon rolls and lingonberry pancakes.

places.name: Pat's Pizza
places.summary: Thin, crackly tavern-style pizza cut into squares, made on Lincoln Avenue since 1950.

places.name: Metro
places.summary: The rock club on Clark Street where generations of bands played on their way up, with Smart Bar dance club in the basement.

places.name: Music Box Theatre
places.summary: 1929 movie palace on Southport with a twinkling ceiling, an organist, repertory and art films.

places.name: Sidetrack
places.summary: Huge Northalsted gay bar with video screens, show-tune nights and a rooftop.

places.name: Intelligentsia Coffee (Broadway)
places.summary: The original cafe of the Chicago roaster, on Broadway near Belmont.

places.name: Lakeview YMCA
places.summary: A neighborhood Y on Marshfield with a pool, classes and an older, friendly membership.

places.name: The 606 (Bloomingdale Trail)
places.summary: An old elevated rail line turned into a trail for joggers, bikes and strollers, running west to Humboldt Park.

places.name: Myopic Books
places.summary: Three cramped floors of used books on Milwaukee Avenue, quiet by house rule.

places.name: Big Star
places.summary: Taqueria and whiskey bar in an old gas station across from the Damen Blue Line, with a crowded summer patio.

places.name: The Violet Hour
places.summary: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar behind a mural-covered wall with no sign, with high-backed chairs and house rules.

places.name: The Map Room
places.summary: Bucktown travelers' tavern with a deep beer list, maps and globes, and coffee in the mornings.

places.name: Wormhole Coffee
places.summary: Milwaukee Avenue coffee shop decorated with 1980s movie props, including a DeLorean.

places.name: Midtown Athletic Club
places.summary: A large club on Elston Avenue with indoor tennis, pools and a rooftop.

places.name: Subterranean
places.summary: A two-level club near the six corners for indie bands, hip-hop and open mics.

places.name: Empty Bottle
places.summary: The scuffed indie and punk club on Western Avenue, with cheap beer and shows most nights.

places.name: Ukrainian National Museum
places.summary: Folk art, pysanky eggs and the history of the community, on Chicago Avenue.

places.name: St. Nicholas Ukrainian Catholic Cathedral
places.summary: A cathedral topped with thirteen copper domes for Christ and the apostles, with Byzantine mosaics inside.

places.name: Ann's Bakery & Deli
places.summary: Ukrainian bakery and deli for poppy-seed rolls, pierogi and smoked meats to take home.

places.name: Rainbo Club
places.summary: An old Division Street dive with a photo booth and a long history with local artists and musicians.

places.name: Star Lounge Coffee Bar
places.summary: Neighborhood espresso bar on Chicago Avenue with a pressed-tin ceiling.

places.name: Sportsman's Club
places.summary: A corner tavern on Chicago Avenue with a tiki-lit back patio and a short list of cocktails.

places.name: Lula Cafe
places.summary: The neighborhood restaurant that helped make Logan Square a food destination, seasonal and relaxed since 1999.

places.name: Longman & Eagle
places.summary: Whiskey-heavy gastropub with rooms upstairs and a long brunch.

places.name: Logan Theatre
places.summary: A restored 1915 neighborhood cinema with cheap tickets and a bar in the lobby.

places.name: Logan Square Farmers Market
places.summary: Sunday market on the boulevard with produce, tamales and live music, moving indoors in winter.

places.name: Illinois Centennial Monument
places.summary: The eagle-topped column at the center of the square, ringed by boulevards and greystones.

places.name: Revolution Brewing Brewpub
places.summary: The local brewery's first pub on Milwaukee Avenue, with raised-fist tap handles and bacon-fat popcorn.

places.name: The Whistler
places.summary: Small cocktail bar with free live jazz and experimental music most nights.

places.name: Humboldt Park
places.summary: A 200-acre park with a lagoon, Prairie-style boathouse, rose garden and summer barbecues blasting salsa and reggaeton.

places.name: Humboldt Park Beach
places.summary: An inland swimming lagoon with a sand beach and lifeguards in summer.

places.name: Paseo Boricua
places.summary: Division Street between two 59-foot steel Puerto Rican flags, lined with murals, bakeries and social clubs.

places.name: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture
places.summary: Exhibitions and classes in the park's old horse stables.

places.name: Café Colao
places.summary: Puerto Rican bakery on Division for café con leche, quesitos and pastelillos.

places.name: Papa's Cache Sabroso
places.summary: Counter-service Puerto Rican food, best known for the jibarito made with fried plantains for bread.

places.name: Girl & the Goat
places.summary: Stephanie Izard's loud, shareable-plates room that set off Randolph Street's restaurant boom.

places.name: Au Cheval
places.summary: Diner-style bar with a famous double cheeseburger and long waits.

places.name: Time Out Market Chicago
places.summary: A Fulton Market food hall of local chefs' stalls with a rooftop bar.

places.name: Lou Mitchell's
places.summary: A Route 66 breakfast diner near Union Station since 1923 that hands out Milk Duds and donut holes to the queue.

places.name: Sawada Coffee
places.summary: Military-latte coffee bar in a warehouse off Green Street.

places.name: Chicago Union Station
places.summary: The Beaux-Arts Great Hall under a barrel-vault skylight, still busy with Amtrak and Metra.

places.name: United Center
places.summary: Arena of the Bulls and Blackhawks, with the Michael Jordan statue out front and big touring concerts.

places.name: Haymarket Pub & Brewery
places.summary: Brewpub near the site of the 1886 Haymarket rally, with beer brewed on site.

places.name: Mario's Italian Lemonade
places.summary: A summer-only Taylor Street stand scooping Italian ice since 1954, with a line on hot evenings.

places.name: Al's #1 Italian Beef (Taylor Street)
places.summary: The original Al's counter, where people eat beef sandwiches standing at the ledge in the "Italian stance".

places.name: Jim's Original
places.summary: Walk-up stand by the expressway serving Maxwell Street Polish sausages with grilled onions and free fries, nearly around the clock.

places.name: Conte di Savoia
places.summary: Italian grocery and deli on Taylor Street for imported pasta, cheeses and sub sandwiches.

places.name: Jane Addams Hull-House Museum
places.summary: The settlement house of the social reformer, now on the UIC campus, with free tours and soup lunches.

places.name: Tufano's Vernon Park Tap
places.summary: A family-run red-sauce tavern since the 1930s, with chalkboard specials and old-neighborhood regulars.

places.name: Maxwell Street Market
places.summary: The descendant of the old open-air market where Chicago blues was played on the street, now a Sunday market of tools, clothes and tacos.

places.name: National Museum of Mexican Art
places.summary: A free museum in Harrison Park with a large collection and a famous Day of the Dead exhibition every autumn.

places.name: 18th Street murals
places.summary: Murals on viaducts, schools and storefronts along 16th and 18th streets, from Aztec themes to labor history.

places.name: Café Jumping Bean
places.summary: Long-running 18th Street coffeehouse covered in local art, with tortas and chess players.

places.name: Carnitas Uruapan
places.summary: Family-run since 1975, selling carnitas by the pound with tortillas, salsa and chicharrón.

places.name: Thalia Hall
places.summary: An 1892 Bohemian opera hall at 18th and Allport, restored for concerts.

places.name: Pilsen Community Books
places.summary: Used and new bookshop on 18th Street with readings and a strong Latinx shelf.

places.name: Little Village Arch
places.summary: The tiled "Bienvenidos a Little Village" arch with its clock over 26th Street.

places.name: 26th Street
places.summary: A mile of quinceañera dress shops, botas, paleterías and the Discount Mall, busiest on weekends.

places.name: Taquería El Milagro
places.summary: Cafeteria-style tacos and tamales beside the tortilla factory on 26th Street.

places.name: Douglass Park
places.summary: A big West Side park with a lagoon and soccer fields busy every weekend.

places.name: Mi Tierra
places.summary: Big family restaurant on 26th with mariachis on weekend nights and enormous margaritas.

places.name: Ping Tom Memorial Park
places.summary: Riverside park with a pagoda, a water taxi stop and dragon boats in summer.

places.name: Ping Tom Park Fieldhouse
places.summary: Park district fieldhouse with an indoor pool, gym and cheap classes.

places.name: Chinatown Gate and Wentworth Avenue
places.summary: The red gate at Cermak and Wentworth, with herbalists, bakeries and the Pui Tak Center beyond.

places.name: Chinatown Square
places.summary: Two-story outdoor mall with zodiac statues, bubble tea, hot pot and karaoke.

places.name: Chiu Quon Bakery
places.summary: Wentworth Avenue bakery since 1986 for egg tarts, pineapple buns and barbecue pork buns.

places.name: MingHin Cuisine
places.summary: Busy Cantonese room with weekend dim sum carts of dumplings and turnip cakes.

places.name: Lao Sze Chuan
places.summary: Fiery Sichuan dishes like dry chili chicken, a Chinatown staple.

places.name: Chinatown Branch Library
places.summary: A rounded glass library with a central atrium, open since 2015.

places.name: Field Museum
places.summary: Natural history on the lakefront: Sue the T. rex, the Egyptian tomb and halls of dioramas.

places.name: Shedd Aquarium
places.summary: Lakefront aquarium with beluga whales, a Caribbean reef and a view back to the skyline.

places.name: Adler Planetarium
places.summary: Planetarium at the end of the Museum Campus peninsula, with the best skyline view in the city.

places.name: Soldier Field
places.summary: The Bears' lakefront stadium inside its old colonnades, also home to the Chicago Fire.

places.name: 12th Street Beach
places.summary: A small curving beach behind the Adler, quieter than the North Side beaches.

places.name: Buddy Guy's Legends
places.summary: Blues club on Wabash owned by the guitarist, with Cajun food and bands every night.

places.name: Jazz Showcase
places.summary: A serious jazz room near Dearborn Station that has booked touring greats since 1947.

places.name: Glessner House
places.summary: A fortress-like 1887 Richardson house on Prairie Avenue, once the city's millionaires' row.

places.name: Eleven City Diner
places.summary: Jewish deli and diner on Wabash with pastrami, matzo ball soup and egg creams.

places.name: Victory Monument
places.summary: Memorial to the Black 8th Illinois regiment of the First World War, at 35th and King Drive.

places.name: Bronzeville Walk of Fame
places.summary: Plaques along King Drive honoring Louis Armstrong, Ida B. Wells, Gwendolyn Brooks and other residents.

places.name: Chicago Bee Branch Library
places.summary: A public library in the art deco home of the Chicago Bee, a Black newspaper of the 1920s.

places.name: Peach's Restaurant
places.summary: Southern breakfast on 47th Street: shrimp and grits, salmon croquettes and a weekend crowd after church.

places.name: Gallery Guichard
places.summary: Gallery of art from the African diaspora on 47th Street, with openings that turn into parties.

places.name: 31st Street Beach
places.summary: A family beach by the harbor, with a pier, picnic lawns and a cafe in the beach house.

places.name: Museum of Science and Industry
places.summary: The last big building of the 1893 World's Fair, holding a coal mine, a German U-boat and a working tornado.

places.name: Frederick C. Robie House
places.summary: Frank Lloyd Wright's long, low Prairie house on the university campus, open for tours.

places.name: Promontory Point
places.summary: A stepped limestone peninsula for swimming off the rocks, bonfires and a long skyline view north.

places.name: Seminary Co-op Bookstores
places.summary: The scholarly co-op bookstore and 57th Street Books, the neighborhood's two serious bookshops.

places.name: Plein Air Cafe
places.summary: Light-filled cafe next to the Robie House, with students and lecturers on laptops.

places.name: Medici on 57th
places.summary: Carved-up wooden booths, pizza, burgers and a bakery next door, a student haunt since 1963.

places.name: Valois Restaurant
places.summary: A 53rd Street cafeteria ("See Your Food") with cheap breakfast, a long counter and everyone from cops to professors.

places.name: ISAC Museum
places.summary: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Near East, with a 40-ton winged bull from Khorsabad.

places.name: DuSable Black History Museum
places.summary: One of the oldest museums of African American history, in Washington Park.

places.name: Jackson Park and the Garden of the Phoenix
places.summary: Olmsted's lagoons and wooded island from the 1893 fair, with a Japanese garden.

places.name: Rate Field
places.summary: The White Sox ballpark at 35th Street, long called Comiskey and then Guaranteed Rate Field, with Maxwell Street Polishes at the stands.

places.name: Maria's Packaged Goods & Community Bar
places.summary: A liquor store in front and a craft-beer bar in back, a model of the new Bridgeport.

places.name: Bridgeport Coffee
places.summary: A corner coffee shop on Morgan Street that roasts its own beans.

places.name: The Duck Inn
places.summary: Tavern-meets-restaurant with a rotisserie duck and a duck-fat hot dog.

places.name: Palmisano Park
places.summary: A former limestone quarry turned into a park with a fishing pond, terraced paths and a hilltop skyline view.

places.name: Ramova Theatre
places.summary: A 1929 Spanish-style movie palace on Halsted, reopened as a music venue with a brewery and the old grill next door.

places.name: Swedish American Museum
places.summary: Small museum on Clark Street about Swedish immigrants, with a children's museum upstairs.

places.name: Hopleaf
places.summary: Belgian beer bar with a long list, mussels and frites and no kids allowed.

places.name: Women & Children First
places.summary: A feminist bookstore since 1979, with readings and a strong LGBTQ+ section.

places.name: The Coffee Studio
places.summary: Small, serious coffee bar on Clark Street with seats in the window.

places.name: Big Jones
places.summary: Southern heritage cooking with a well-loved brunch of beignets and fried chicken.

places.name: Simon's Tavern
places.summary: Old Swedish tavern with a neon fish sign that serves its own glögg in winter.

places.name: Green Mill Cocktail Lounge
places.summary: A 1907 jazz lounge where Capone had a booth, with live jazz nightly and the Uptown Poetry Slam on Sundays.

places.name: Aragon Ballroom
places.summary: A 1926 Spanish-courtyard ballroom with a starry ceiling, now for big rock and electronic shows.

places.name: Riviera Theatre
places.summary: A former movie palace at Broadway and Lawrence hosting mid-size concerts.

places.name: Montrose Beach and the Magic Hedge
places.summary: The city's biggest beach, with a dog beach, a fishing pier and a bird sanctuary famous for spring migration.

places.name: Tank Noodle
places.summary: Big, busy pho and bánh mì restaurant at Argyle and Broadway.

climate.summary: Humid continental: long, cold, windy winters with lake-effect snow, a short spring, hot and humid summers with thunderstorms, and a crisp, golden autumn. The lake keeps the shore cooler in spring and summer.

months.note: Bitter cold and wind off the lake; subzero snaps and snow most weeks.
Still frozen; the lake edge piles up with ice.
Raw and changeable; a spring storm can still bring heavy snow.
Cool and wet; cold lake breezes along the shore.
Patios and beaches open; it can be 80 inland and 55 by the lake.
Hottest month; muggy heat waves and crowded beaches.
Hot and humid; the lake is warmest for swimming.
Warm days, cooler nights; the best weather of the year.
Crisp; leaves turn and the first frost arrives.
Gray and windy; the first snow flurries.
Cold, dark and snowy; the Hawk wind arrives.

annual_events.name: St. Patrick's Day river dyeing and parade
annual_events.summary: The river is dyed bright green on the Saturday before St. Patrick's Day, followed by a parade on Columbus Drive.

annual_events.name: Cubs Opening Day
annual_events.summary: Wrigleyville bars open at dawn for the first home game, often in snow flurries.

annual_events.name: Chicago Blues Festival
annual_events.summary: Free blues festival in Millennium Park, the largest of its kind.

annual_events.name: Printers Row Lit Fest
annual_events.summary: Book tents, author talks and used-book dealers along Dearborn Street.

annual_events.name: Chicago Pride Parade and Pride Fest
annual_events.summary: Northalsted street fest and a huge Sunday parade through Lakeview.

annual_events.name: Puerto Rican People's Parade and Fiesta Boricua
annual_events.summary: Parade, music and food in and around Humboldt Park, with flags on every car.

annual_events.name: Grant Park Music Festival
annual_events.summary: Free classical concerts at the Pritzker Pavilion, with picnics on the lawn.

annual_events.name: Lollapalooza
annual_events.summary: Four days of rock, pop and EDM across Grant Park in late July or early August.

annual_events.name: Chicago Air and Water Show
annual_events.summary: Jets and stunt planes over North Avenue Beach, rattling windows all along the lakefront.

annual_events.name: Chicago Jazz Festival
annual_events.summary: Free jazz festival in Millennium Park over Labor Day weekend.

annual_events.name: 26th Street Mexican Independence Day Parade
annual_events.summary: Floats, horses, flags and honking cars on 26th Street around September 16.

annual_events.name: Taste of Chicago
annual_events.summary: Food stalls from local restaurants in Grant Park; long a July event, it now usually runs in September.

annual_events.name: Chicago Marathon
annual_events.summary: A flat, fast course through 29 neighborhoods from Grant Park, with crowds cheering in Pilsen, Chinatown and Boystown.

annual_events.name: Open House Chicago
annual_events.summary: A weekend of free entry to buildings normally closed to the public, from penthouses to churches.

annual_events.name: Magnificent Mile Lights Festival
annual_events.summary: A parade and the lighting of the trees along Michigan Avenue the weekend before Thanksgiving.

annual_events.name: Christkindlmarket
annual_events.summary: German-style Christmas market in Daley Plaza with mulled wine in collectable boot mugs.

annual_events.name: ZooLights
annual_events.summary: Millions of lights across Lincoln Park Zoo on winter evenings.

annual_events.name: Bears football season
annual_events.summary: Sunday game days, tailgates in the Soldier Field lots and Monday moods across the city.

local_color.name: Deep-dish pizza
local_color.summary: A tall, buttery crust baked in a pan, filled with cheese and sausage and topped with chunky tomato sauce; locals eat it for visitors and occasions more than every week.

local_color.name: Tavern-style pizza
local_color.summary: The pizza Chicagoans actually eat most: thin, crackly crust cut into squares ("party cut"), and the corner pieces are fought over.

local_color.name: Italian beef
local_color.summary: Thin-sliced roast beef soaked in jus on a long roll, topped with sweet peppers or hot giardiniera; order it "dipped" or "wet" and eat it leaning over the counter.

local_color.name: Chicago-style hot dog
local_color.summary: An all-beef dog on a poppy-seed bun "dragged through the garden": yellow mustard, neon relish, onion, tomato, pickle spear, sport peppers and celery salt. Never ketchup.

local_color.name: Maxwell Street Polish
local_color.summary: A grilled Polish sausage with grilled onions and mustard, from the old Maxwell Street market.

local_color.name: Jibarito
local_color.summary: A Chicago Puerto Rican invention: steak, garlic mayo, lettuce and tomato between two flattened fried plantains.

local_color.name: Pączki Day
local_color.summary: On Fat Tuesday, Polish bakeries sell out of rich filled doughnuts (pączki) from before dawn, and offices fill with boxes of them.

local_color.name: Chicago Mix popcorn
local_color.summary: Caramel and cheese popcorn mixed in one bag, sold by Garrett Popcorn shops downtown with lines out the door.

local_color.name: Malört
local_color.summary: A bitter wormwood liqueur that locals pour for visitors to watch their faces, then drink themselves as a point of pride.

local_color.name: Old Style
local_color.summary: The cheap lager on corner-tavern signs and at Wrigley for decades; tall cans of it signal an old-school bar.

local_color.name: "The Bean"
local_color.summary: Nobody calls Anish Kapoor's Cloud Gate by its name; it is the Bean, and meeting "at the Bean" is a standard plan downtown.

local_color.name: Dibs
local_color.summary: After a snowstorm, people who dig out a street parking space claim it with a lawn chair, a cone or an old ironing board, and moving someone's dibs starts feuds.

local_color.name: "The L"
local_color.summary: The trains are the L, whether elevated or underground, and lines go by color; directions are given as "take the Red to Belmont".

local_color.name: "Lake Shore Drive"
local_color.summary: The lakefront highway is still Lake Shore Drive to locals, officially renamed for Jean Baptiste Point DuSable in 2021, and directions are given as "the lake is east".

local_color.name: "The Hawk"
local_color.summary: The bitter winter wind off the lake, as in "the Hawk is out today".

local_color.name: "Pop", "Jewels" and "the Ryan"
local_color.summary: Soda is pop, Jewel-Osco is "the Jewels", and expressways go by names: the Kennedy, the Dan Ryan, the Eisenhower.

local_color.name: Cubs or Sox
local_color.summary: Baseball loyalty roughly follows the city map: the North Side for the Cubs, the South Side for the White Sox, and switching sides is not done.

local_color.name: Lakefront summer
local_color.summary: The first warm weekend, everyone heads to the lake: beaches, the trail, volleyball and grills along twenty-six miles of mostly public shore.

local_color.name: Chicago Cubs
local_color.summary: The North Side baseball team at Wrigley Field, whose 2016 World Series ended a 108-year wait; fans sing "Go Cubs Go" after wins and fly a W flag.

local_color.name: Chicago White Sox
local_color.summary: The South Side baseball team in Bridgeport, with a working-class, no-nonsense fan base.

local_color.name: Chicago Bears
local_color.summary: "Da Bears": the NFL team at Soldier Field, followed with grim devotion through long, cold seasons.

local_color.name: Bulls and Blackhawks
local_color.summary: The basketball and hockey teams share the United Center; the Jordan-era Bulls and the 2010s Blackhawks are still talked about.

local_color.name: Blues and improv
local_color.summary: Chicago blues came up from the Delta through the South Side, and improv comedy grew up here too; both are still played nightly.
